description: Cross-document synthesis gold for the consolidation Value A/B (Track 2c). Each question requires facts spread across >=2 engram corpus docs (ARCHITECTURE.md + CLAUDE.md, plus eval/RESULTS.md for sg12), so flat single-chunk retrieval (Arm B) is disadvantaged relative to the consolidated drill_down summary (Arm A). Ground truth is the human-authored answer key; judging is blind 0-2 against it.

questions.question: What are engram's two execution planes, and why must an HTTP handler that embeds wrap its work in spawn_blocking while never holding the write lock across network I/O?
questions.ground_truth: Hot path = async axum handlers; cold path = dedicated std::thread OS threads (jobs workers + tree sweeper). The embedder and LLM/audit calls use reqwest::blocking, so any handler that embeds (ingest_doc, query_docs, tree_query) must wrap the work in tokio::task::spawn_blocking or it stalls the runtime. Separately, the off-lock invariant computes embeddings/summaries BEFORE taking the write mutex, so the lock is never held across network I/O.

questions.question: How does the job queue make re-ingesting a document idempotent, and what is the job_id format?
questions.ground_truth: job_id = "{namespace}:{document_id}", so re-ingesting the same doc re-enqueues the same job and the ON CONFLICT clause resets it to pending. One job per document; claim_job atomically flips pending->running and increments attempts.

questions.question: What are the three gates that can seal a buffer during the consolidation cascade, and how does the L0 gate differ from the L>=1 gate?
questions.ground_truth: L0 seals when the summed approx-tokens (chars/4) of its leaves reach seal_input_token_budget. L>=1 seals when the sibling count reaches seal_fanout. The third is a stale-flush age gate (seal_flush_age_secs). The cascade recurses upward to MAX_CASCADE_DEPTH = 32.

questions.question: Is the forget path (DELETE by-key) a complete erasure of a document's text?
questions.ground_truth: No. delete_doc_by_key atomically removes the doc + chunks + entities + pending job + unsealed L0 leaves, but NOT sealed summary nodes. A forgotten doc's text can still live inside sealed summary bodies (and the write-only vault). Sealed tree nodes are immutable.

questions.question: Why must engram's SQLite DB live on native ext4 rather than the repo's v9fs mount, and what does deploy do about it?
questions.ground_truth: The repo lives on a Windows v9fs mount where WAL is flaky and chmod doesn't stick. Deploy keeps the DB, vault, logs, and .env (chmod 600) under $HOME/engram on ext4, and ENGRAM_DB should point at an ext4 path. (cargo test is fine — it uses system tempdirs.)

questions.question: What happens to existing chunks if you change ENGRAM_EMBED_MODEL or ENGRAM_EMBED_DIM, and why?
questions.ground_truth: Each embedder's signature (e.g. gateway:mxbai-embed-large:1024) is stored on every chunk/tree node and reads filter by it. Changing the model or dim makes all existing chunks invisible/orphaned (not migrated) — a full re-ingest is required.

questions.question: How does search_code's path-prior and definition-boost differ from the 0.55 graph signal that was kept off, and what does each do to ranking?
questions.ground_truth: The path-type ranking prior down-weights docs/tests/config/LICENSE so source ranks first; the definition boost (ENGRAM_CODE_DEF_BOOST, 0.10, IDF-gated) favours the file defining a rare query symbol, fixing definition-vs-usage burial. The 0.55-weight sym:-graph blend, by contrast, was measured to HURT code recall and ships off (ENGRAM_CODE_GRAPH=false). Path-prior + def-boost help; the graph signal cratered recall.

questions.question: What are engram's embedder implementations and which one is used in production versus tests?
questions.ground_truth: The Embedder trait has HashEmbedder (deterministic, tests-only), OllamaEmbedder, and GatewayEmbedder (prod, model mxbai-embed-large, dim 1024, via the litellm gateway). There is also a FallbackEmbedder wrapper (primary + fallback). Production uses GatewayEmbedder (optionally wrapped in FallbackEmbedder); tests use HashEmbedder.

questions.question: What does requeue_running do and when does it run?
questions.ground_truth: requeue_running runs at startup (crash recovery) and returns any job orphaned in the running state back to pending, so jobs interrupted by a crash are re-processed. It is invoked from main.rs after Store::open.

questions.question: When FallbackEmbedder wraps the primary with a local failover, why does a failover never orphan chunks under a different signature?
questions.ground_truth: FallbackEmbedder's signature() delegates to the primary embedder. So even when the local OllamaEmbedder failover actually produces a vector, the chunk is still stamped with the primary's signature — reads filter by that one signature and the failover never orphans chunks under a divergent signature.

questions.question: What are engram's two chunking modes and how is each dispatched?
questions.ground_truth: Prose mode (default): paragraph split on \n\n packed to ~800 chars (CJK-safe), entities via mechanical regex (email:/url:/handle:/hashtag:). Code mode: dispatched on meta.kind=="file"; tree-sitter function/type-boundary chunking (10 langs) plus AST sym:/import:/path: extraction, falling back to the heuristic chunk_code on unsupported langs or parse failure.

questions.question: Why was the 0.55-weight sym:-graph signal kept off in search_code, with reference to its measured effect on recall@5?
questions.ground_truth: The sym:-graph blend was measured to HURT code recall, cratering recall@5 to 0.600 — worse than the no-graph baseline. That is why ENGRAM_CODE_GRAPH ships off. search_code instead relies on vector + IDF-weighted keyword + path-prior + def-boost. (Production tree-sitter config: recall@5 0.771.)

questions.question: Which specific functions enforce the off-lock invariant on the ingest path and on the consolidation path?
questions.ground_truth: On ingest: ingest_document embeds each chunk off-lock, then commit_ingest performs the atomic write. On consolidation: tree::seal_cascade summarizes + embeds off-lock, then seal_buffer performs the atomic node/edge write. Neither holds the write mutex across network I/O.

questions.question: When a prose doc is consolidated, which trees does process_doc fan its chunks out into, and how is each keyed?
questions.ground_truth: For prose, process_doc fans level-0 leaves into: a Source tree (tree_key = author), the Global tree (tree_key = "global"), and one Topic tree per entity (tree_key = the entity id). Code mode instead uses a directory-keyed module tree + global + topic trees on sym:/import: entities, gated off by default.

questions.question: How does the architecture/module digest path differ from the consolidation tree, and why was the single-pass approach chosen?
questions.ground_truth: get_architecture/get_module serve a cached SINGLE-PASS digest from <ns>:meta (one LLM summary over the repo's source), built by rebuild_architecture_digest; the consolidation-tree drill is only a fallback when no digest is cached. A single compression pass preserves specifics that the deep summary-of-summaries fold loses (measured: one-shot 1.58 vs tree 1.08 of 2).

questions.question: What does commit_ingest write atomically, and why is it wrapped in a transaction?
questions.ground_truth: commit_ingest writes the doc + chunks + entities + the consolidation job enqueue (and code edges) in one transaction, so a crash can't leave a partial state. There are no FK constraints — referential integrity is upheld by these multi-statement transactions (commit_ingest, seal_buffer, delete_chunks_for_doc, claim_job).

questions.question: How is the storage layer split between reads and writes, and what SQLite settings make concurrent readers safe with the single writer?
questions.ground_truth: Store holds read: an r2d2 pool (up to 8 connections) and write: an Arc<Mutex<Connection>> — all writes go through the one mutexed connection, reads come from the pool. WAL mode (journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, busy_timeout=15s) lets readers run concurrently with the writer. Store is Clone (it clones the Arcs).

questions.question: What are the three namespaces a repo maps onto, and what does each hold?
questions.ground_truth: repo:<id> — the file documents + their chunks/symbols (the searchable code). repo:<id>:history — git commits (meta.kind="commit"), backing why. repo:<id>:meta — the single conventions/architecture digest doc (key conventions / architecture / module:<dir>).

questions.question: How does search_code's keyword signal differ from prose query keyword scoring, and what does the IDF re-rank achieve?
questions.ground_truth: search_code is chunk-level (not doc-level) and uses IDF-weighted keyword scoring (ENGRAM_CODE_KEYWORD_IDF, default on) at weight ENGRAM_CODE_KW_WEIGHT (0.50), so rare query terms dominate ranking; prose query uses plain keyword in a vector/keyword (or graph) blend. The IDF re-rank makes rare identifiers the dominant ranking signal in code search.

questions.question: Why does the cold path run on dedicated std::thread OS threads instead of tokio tasks, and what do those threads do?
questions.ground_truth: jobs::spawn_workers and tree::spawn_sweeper run on dedicated std::thread OS threads (not tokio tasks), driven from main.rs, because they call blocking HTTP directly (no spawn_blocking needed there). Workers drain the post_acquire_jobs queue; the sweeper periodically seals stale buffers. Both share a stop: Arc<AtomicBool>.
